prompt_html: Which are the correct breakeven prices for the underlying for a short strangle strategy at the $100.00 and $110.00 strike prices in which the call option premium collected was $5.50 and the put option premium was $4.50 when the underlying traded at $100.50?

What is the profit on a short strangle strategy given the following information? With the underlying share price trading at $67.50, an investor writes (sells) the $60.00/$65.00 strangle expiring in 90-days and collects a total premium of $3.75. At expiration the underlying settles at $61.25.
Which of the following is a possible reason for an option investor to sell a short strangle strategy?
choices_html: The share price is expected to either rise sharply or fall precipitously over the life of the option contract.
The investor is extremely bearish on the outlook for the stock over the life of the option contract.
